source.check: every figure read from the two page images: the Newry Telegraph prints Trainor 940, Richardson 770, spoiled 20 (the same figures in the Newry Reporter, 15 June 1961, p. 5)

note: Triennial election of the county council, 1961: nominations closed 16 May 1961; 21 of the 22 seats returned unopposed and one contest, Crossmaglen, polled 1 June 1961. The unopposed list prints no party labels. Trainor took the seat from Richardson, member for the division for 16 years. The Armagh Guardian (8 June 1961, p. 4) gives 1,730 votes recorded including 20 spoiled, an electorate of 2,004, a majority of 170 and Trainor's vote as 970; 970 does not fit its own totals, so the Newry Telegraph's 940 and 770 (summing to the 1,710 valid votes) are used. The nominations report prints the names Edward J. Richardson and Malachy Traynor. No party labels printed.
